name: Headless mode (claude -p)
summary: Run Claude Code from scripts and CI with a single command that prints its answer and exits.
what: Adding -p (short for --print) to the claude command runs one task without the interactive screen. Claude works on the prompt, prints the result and exits, so you can call it from a shell script, a Git hook or a CI job. You choose which tools it may use without asking, and can get the result as plain text, JSON or a stream of events.

impact.title: Automate routine tasks
impact.detail: Fix lint errors, write release notes or review a diff as one step of a script or pipeline.

impact.title: Output your tools can read
impact.detail: JSON output includes the result and a session id, and a JSON Schema can make Claude return data in an exact shape.

impact.title: Safe unattended runs
impact.detail: Pre-approve only the tools a task needs; anything else is refused instead of waiting for a person.

howItWorks: Run claude -p "your task" and the answer is printed to the terminal.
Allow tools up front with --allowedTools, for example "Read,Edit,Bash(git diff *)".
Pick the format with --output-format: text (the default), json or stream-json.
Continue a run with --continue, or a specific one with --resume and its session id.
Check the exit code: 0 means success, anything else a failure.

events.note: Already part of Claude Code when the changelog began with this version.
Print mode can stream its output with --output-format=stream-json.
